text:
marta: Quick update — we rolled out the new quant-aware batching + prefix KV cache to the small-gen model family in prod at 08:00 PT (rolled 3 regions, canary -> gradual). Short summary: p50 token latency down ~15%, p95 down ~18%, p99 down ~12% on average; overall per-token cost down ~22% on these workloads. Observed particularly strong wins on short-turn dialogues where cache hits are frequent.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: quant-batching-v3 -> canary (3% traffic) -> gradual (3 regions). All healthchecks passed in canary window.

ev an: Nice! What were the rollback/alert criteria for the canary?

marta: Canary checks were: p99 tail latency spike >25% vs baseline OR error rate increase >0.2% OR model output regressions flagged by eval set. We also had an automated fallback to previous kernel (zero-downtime) if any of the checks tripped. We didn't hit any of those.

kevin: Do we have a simple snippet of the runtime config that changed? Want to replicate locally for perf tests.

marta: Yep — here's the minimal config we pushed (prod varies per-region):

```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_size: 48
  max_wait_ms: 12
  prefer_sequence_grouping: true
  quant_aware: true
cache:
  prefix_kv_cache: true
  ttl_seconds: 600
  cache_shards: 8
kernel_selection:
  prefer_int8_kernels: true
  fallback_to_fp16: true
```

marta: Notes: the key is mixing quant_aware batching with small max_wait_ms so short requests don't wait long, plus prefix_kv gives big wins when user turns repeat prefixes. We tuned shard count to avoid lock contention on the cache.

kevin: Did embeddings or rerank endpoints see anything?

marta: Embeddings endpoints were excluded (different runtime pathway). Rerank endpoints saw modest batching benefits but no KV cache wins.

evan: Any regressions in quality observed by the eval suite?

marta: Ran the usual eval corpus (1000 prompts + human checks for top-10 regressions). No regression above threshold. A couple of edge cases with very long prefix concatenations had slightly different tokenization timing but not output quality.

infra-bot: Canary -> gradual completed: 3 regions at ~23:40 PT. No incidents.

sasha: Amazing work, team — big impact. Can you add a short blurb to the internal release notes and perf playbook?

marta: Will do. Draft link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime/quant-batching-2026 (internal only). Also adding a one-pager to the perf playbook with rollout checklist + tuning knobs.

kevin: I'll try to reproduce the ~22% cost drop on my local replay. Any recommended replay settings?

marta: Use real traffic mix if possible. Key tips: preserve inter-arrival timing (very important for caching), use small-turn dialogues to highlight cache effects, and enable quant kernels in the runtime build. If you need a dataset, ping me and I'll share a redacted traffic slice.

evan: Awesome. Thanks for the clear rollout and configs — will propagate the notes to the SRE runbook. :tada:

sasha: tiny question — do we need to notify Dedicated customers about changed perf characteristics?

marta: For Dedicated we exposed the same knobs but left defaults unchanged; we'll recommend the config to customers via account teams and document the expected gains and tradeoffs.

marta: TL;DR: production rollout complete, measurable latency and cost wins, no regressions or incidents. Follow-up: I’ll post detailed dashboards and perf traces in the release notes later today.
